name: Buffer
description: Buffer helps teams plan, publish, and analyze social content across connected channels.
agentUseSummary: Connect one Buffer account through Relay-owned OAuth, then let agents inspect bounded, identity- and content-redacted account structure metadata.

capabilities.label: Read social account structure
capabilities.description: Read bounded, identity- and content-redacted account, organization, and channel lifecycle metadata.

approvalRequired.label: Read Buffer account status
approvalRequired.description: Read account ID, creation date, timezone, and a bounded organization count without identity.

approvalRequired.label: List Buffer organizations
approvalRequired.description: List at most 25 organization IDs and channel counts without names, emails, members, or limits.

approvalRequired.label: List Buffer channel lifecycle
approvalRequired.description: List at most 25 identity-redacted channel lifecycle summaries for one exact organization.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: Every bounded metadata read requires approval; identity, post and idea content, analytics, writes, arbitrary GraphQL, pagination, and raw access remain blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: The same three bounded reads run directly; fixed origin, static GraphQL documents, exact identifiers, redaction, bounds, audits, and provider rate limits remain mandatory.

runtimeSupport.description: Railway mounts only three static, redacted GraphQL metadata reads and injects OAuth tokens server-side.

providerSetup.blocker: A Buffer OAuth client, confidential client credentials, exact Railway callback, S256 PKCE, consent, single-use refresh rotation testing, and live acceptance are required.
providerSetup.nextAction: Use the separate provider-console task to register the app, configure the exact callback and Railway credentials, then validate authorization, rotating refresh, redaction, plan limits, rate-limit handling, disconnect, and post-disconnect denial.

evidence.supports: Official OAuth authorization and token origins, mandatory S256 PKCE for all clients, confidential-client token exchange, one-hour access tokens, offline_access, and single-use rotating refresh tokens.
Official fixed GraphQL API origin and account, organization, and channel query surfaces.
Current API availability, third-party OAuth guidance, and plan-specific request limits.

securityNotes: Relay requests only account:read and offline_access and exposes three approval-gated read-only wrappers.
Account email and name, organization names, owner email, members and limits, and channel identity and content fields are stripped.
Requests use only https://api.buffer.com, reject redirects, send static GraphQL documents, validate exact organization IDs, cap responses at 1 MB, and return at most 25 resources.

Posts, ideas, messages, schedules, drafts, analytics, publishing, engagement, account administration, writes, arbitrary GraphQL, variables beyond exact IDs, pagination, raw APIs, bulk, and exports are unavailable.

Buffer limits requests per 15-minute, 24-hour, and 30-day windows by plan. Relay propagates 429 responses. Refresh tokens are single-use and the replacement must be saved atomically; disconnect is local because the current guide exposes no revocation endpoint.
